chunks: And Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:
"Four are required to perform the prayer in full during travel, whether they are in travel or in residence: al-Mukārī, al-Kariyy, the shepherd, and al-Ashtaqān, because that is their work."
And it was narrated: "The sailor and al-Ashtaqān, the courier."

key_terms.التَّمَامُ: performing the prayer in full, without shortening it
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, in the legal context of journeying
key_terms.الْأَشْتَقَانُ: a professional traveler or courier mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence or being at home rather than traveling
key_terms.الْكَرِيُّ: a hired transport driver whose occupation involves travel
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: a transporter or mule-driver whose work involves travel

ai.seo_question: Who must perform full salat while traveling according to this hadith from Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat during travel for people whose occupation is based on continuous movement and travel. It states that such people perform the prayer in full, because travel is part of their regular work.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1275 - Zurarah narrated from Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) that He said:

"There are four categories of people who are required to offer the full (complete) prayer whether they are traveling or at home: the mule driver (al-Mukari), the camel driver (al-Karri), the shepherd, and al-Ashtaqan (those who constantly travel as part of their work). This is because it is their work (which involves constant travel)."
It was also narrated: "The sailor (al-Mallah) and al-Ashtaqan (a type of courier or mail carrier) are also included."
